description.value: The study examined whether the ventromedial prefrontal cortex encodes subjective emotional value and how cognitive reappraisal of positive and negative affective images changes this signal.

design.value: Two independent experimental samples of human participants performed a cognitive reappraisal task while undergoing fMRI. Exp1 was newly collected, and Exp2 was a replication sample drawn from a previously published study; experimental parameters were nearly identical.

task_description.value: Participants viewed images from the International Affective Picture System and were asked either to regulate their emotions using cognitive reappraisal or to experience their emotions naturally.

instructions.value: For the Experience condition, participants were instructed to experience their emotions naturally. For the Regulate condition, participants were asked to emotionally detach themselves from the image by imagining themselves as an objective observer or imagining the event as having no personal relevance to them.

stimuli.value: Images from the International Affective Picture System, categorized as positive, negative, or neutral based on normative IAPS ratings.

description.value: Functional data were acquired using a gradient-echo inverse-spiral pulse sequence with TR = 2000 ms, TE = 30 ms, FOV = 256 mm, flip angle = 60°, 30 axial slices parallel to the AC–PC plane, and voxel size = 4 × 4 × 4 mm. Each run contained 288 volumes; the first six volumes were discarded.

description.value: Functional data were acquired using the same general gradient-echo inverse-spiral parameters as Exp1, with TR = 2000 ms, TE = 31 ms, flip angle = 90°, 34 slices, and voxel size = 3.75 × 3.75 × 3.8 mm. Each run contained 238 volumes; the first six volumes were discarded.
A high-resolution inversion-recovery prepared SPGR anatomical image was used for normalization and coregistration of the functional data, with whole-brain coverage and 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxels.

A high-resolution inversion-recovery prepared SPGR anatomical image was used for normalization and coregistration of the functional data, with TR = 12.3 ms, TE = 5.5 ms, whole-brain coverage, and 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxels.

fMRI preprocessing included motion correction, brain extraction, spatial smoothing, high-pass filtering, and normalization using transforms estimated from each participant's high-resolution anatomical image and FSL's MNI template.

steps.value: Spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 6 mm FWHM.
Functional images were normalized using transforms estimated from each participant's own high-resolution anatomical image and FSL's MNI template.
Registration to the participant's main structural image used six degrees of freedom, and registration to standard space used 12 degrees of freedom.
Runs with >5 volumes with movement of >1 mm in any direction were discarded.

model_settings.value: One regressor of interest was created for each trial type: Positive-Experience, Negative-Experience, Positive-Regulate, Negative-Regulate, and Neutral-Experience. Regressors modeled the 8 s implementation period in Exp1 and 6 s in Exp2; nuisance regressors modeled the initial picture presentation and response period.
Combined the data across all runs within a single participant.
Valence and condition were modeled as fixed effects and each participant as a random effect; variance components covariance structure.

The amplitude of the event-related response was modulated by participants' ratings for each image. The parametric regressor was orthogonalized to the main effect, and a quadratic regressor was included to control for nonlinear results.

A first-level model was created for each trial for each participant using the 8 s implementation period in Exp1 and 6 s in Exp2. Nuisance regressors modeled all other trials, the initial picture presentation, and the response phase.

Mean-centered IAPS normative ratings and regulation condition were modeled as fixed effects and participant as a random effect; the IAPS normative rating, condition, and their interaction were tested as predictors of pvmPFC activation.

The dependent variable was trial-by-trial valence ratings. Independent variables were experiment number, IAPS normative ratings, condition, the interaction of IAPS normative ratings and condition, and trial-by-trial pvmPFC activation estimates.
